scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

Imported Andorra coverage begins in 1938 and ends in 2020. The historical account starts from the pariatges while recognizing earlier habitation; it does not alter or certify imported geometry. Date basis stays map coverage, with no fictitious fall in 2020.

The Government’s short history incorrectly compresses the 1993 referendum and constitutional entry into force. The card distinguishes referendum approval on March 14 from commencement on official publication, as the Constitution’s final provision requires. Its promulgation text is dated April 28.

The English council introduction also mistranslates the number of constitutional articles as seven. This error is not used. Articles 1, 2, 43 and the final provision were checked in the official text.
Parliamentary sources distinguish the 1419 privilege from the first existence of community assemblies. Elite control, unequal representation and later franchise reversals are explicit.

Casa de la Vall sources differ over the purchase date, 1701 or 1702, including across language versions. The card uses the consistently supported 1702 occupation rather than claiming an exact purchase day. Text describes the site; photographs were not independently inspected.
The Seven Keys cabinet is described as an archival object. No unsupported date for a seventh key or exact access procedure is invented. The 1962 seating arrangement is not presented as medieval.

The Farga Rossell page gives 1842 to 1876, while the route page describes building between 1842 and 1846. The narrative uses mid-nineteenth-century operation and the supported closure year. Reconstructed displays are distinguished from original machinery.
The UNESCO account supports named structures and communal land management. Its idealized descriptions of perfect environmental harmony are not adopted as a universal or measured ecological result.

Casa Rull and Casa Cristo are different household contexts. Museum descriptions and the Culture guide supply the specific examples; the guide’s commercial information and old visitor schedules are not presented as current advice.
The religious-art entry distinguishes original removed murals from contemporary projections. It makes no claim that every mural remained in place, and assigns no invented painter biography.
Modern constitutional continuity is explicit. No conquest, annexation or successor destination is manufactured.
Independent historical review, identity and border verification, and depth certification remain pending.
